title: Threat register
description: Every threat enumerated across a deployment's threat models, as structured rows. The models themselves are prose Markdown -- one per subject, authored to a documented section layout -- so the model file is NOT a contract artifact and cannot be projected. The register is the structured restatement: a parser reads the models and emits this, which is what every threat dashboard and rollup actually consumes. Modelled as a scope-ref aggregate for the same reason corpus-registry is: it restates a whole population rather than describing one run.

version.description: Optional: the emitted register predates a version field, so a consumer must not require one.

meta.description: Provenance of this build. Load-bearing: a register built over a partial or mis-rooted model set looks exactly like a real decline in threats unless `models` is read alongside the counts. This is the shape the producer emits; the flat top-level equivalents are deprecated aliases from v0.17.0.

root.description: Filesystem root the models were read from, on the machine that generated this. Local provenance only -- never a portable identifier, and never a join key.

models.description: Models parsed. A register reporting 0 here is an empty build, not an estate with no threats -- the distinction has already been observed in a stale artifact.

models_skipped_nonconforming.description: Models found but not parseable to the section layout. A rising count means the register is silently narrowing.

scoring.description: The exact impact/likelihood weighting behind `score`, recorded because the number is an ORDERING and not a calibrated risk value. Stating it inline keeps a consumer from reading it as CVSS.

updated.description: When this register was last regenerated. DEPRECATED: published in v0.17.0 on an envelope no producer emits; read `meta` instead. Retained as optional so the correction is not a breaking change.

models.description: How many models were parsed. DEPRECATED: published in v0.17.0 on an envelope no producer emits; read `meta` instead. Retained as optional so the correction is not a breaking change.

models_skipped_nonconforming.description: Models found but not parseable. DEPRECATED: published in v0.17.0 on an envelope no producer emits; read `meta` instead. Retained as optional so the correction is not a breaking change.

scoring.description: The impact/likelihood weighting behind `score`. DEPRECATED: published in v0.17.0 on an envelope no producer emits; read `meta` instead. Retained as optional so the correction is not a breaking change.

key.description: Stable identity of this threat across regenerations: the model's subject path plus the in-model id. The in-model `id` alone is NOT unique -- every model numbers from T1.

id.description: In-model identifier, unique only within its own model.

model.description: Path of the threat model this row was parsed from. The provenance link back to the prose.

subject_id.description: The subject this model covers, matching artifact_binding.subject_id. Supplied when the register is built against a resolved corpus; without it a threat cannot be joined to ownership.

actors.description: Actor classes that can drive this threat. See enums/v1/actor-kind.json.

impact.description: See enums/v1/threat-impact.json. Deliberately NOT the finding severity enum: a threat is modelled before it is known to be reachable, and 'existential' has no severity counterpart.

status.description: See enums/v1/threat-status.json. 'partially_mitigated' is its own state and must never be folded into 'mitigated' -- it is the largest bucket in practice, so collapsing it overstates coverage more than any other single choice here.

controls.description: Controls asserted to bear on this threat, as written in the model.

evidence.description: Finding or validation identifiers backing this threat. An empty list means the threat is modelled but not evidenced, which is a different claim from being unmitigated.

linddun.description: Whether this row came from the LINDDUN privacy lens rather than the security lens.

score.description: impact weight x likelihood weight. An ORDERING for triage queues only -- never a calibrated risk figure, and never comparable to CVSS. The weights are recorded in `scoring`.

isolation_dimensions.description: PEACH isolation dimensions this threat touches, when the isolation lens was applied.

isolation_boundaries.description: Tenancy boundaries this threat crosses, when the isolation lens was applied.
